neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x4. Good historian.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Tongue midline with mild left-sided fasciculations. No dysarthria. Jaw jerk mildly brisk.
neurological_exam.motor: Left arm: shoulder abduction 4/5, elbow flexion 4/5, hand intrinsic 3+/5, thenar atrophy visible. Right arm: 4+/5 throughout. Bilateral leg: mild hip flexor weakness 4+/5, otherwise 5/5. Visible fasciculations bilateral arms.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps 3+ bilaterally, brachioradialis 3+. Knee jerks 3+. Ankle jerks 2+. Hoffman bilateral. Left Babinski positive.

neurological_exam.additional: HIV-positive patient; vacuolar myelopathy (HIV myelopathy) is in the differential but clinical features suggest superimposed ALS.

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive arm and leg weakness over 10 months in HIV-positive patient on ART
patient.history_present_illness:
Ms. T is a 46-year-old woman living with HIV on antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load presenting with 10-month progressive arm and leg weakness. She was diagnosed with HIV 12 years ago and has been stably treated on bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide for 3 years with consistently undetectable viral load and CD4 count >500 cells/uL.

She first noticed left arm weakness and wasting 10 months ago and was initially referred to HIV neurology given concern for HIV-related complications. However, the pattern of weakness with visible muscle twitching and fasciculations, combined with hyperreflexia and a Babinski sign, is not typical of HIV myelopathy (vacuolar myelopathy) or HIV-associated neuropathy.

Her HIV neurologist considered HIV vacuolar myelopathy, CMV radiculopathy, and lymphoma as possible etiologies. MRI spine was obtained and showed no vacuolar changes, no cord compression, no lymphoma. CD4 count 520 cells/uL argues against opportunistic CNS processes. The fasciculations in arms and the left tongue, combined with combined UMN and LMN signs, raised the question of ALS in an HIV-positive patient.

signal_characteristics.T2: No vacuolar change, no signal abnormality

additional_observations: No HIV vacuolar myelopathy pattern (posterior column T2 change typically)
mri.impression: No HIV vacuolar myelopathy (typically posterior column changes). No cord compression. No CNS lymphoma. Clinical correlation recommended.

abnormal_values_summary: JC seropositive (PML risk low given CD4 and MRI)

findings.finding: Left FDI, APB: fibrillations +2, complex fasciculation potentials, large MUPs, reduced recruitment. Right FDI: fasciculations complex, sparse fibrillations. Cervical paraspinals: fibrillations +1.
Right tibialis anterior: fasciculations, mildly large MUPs. Sparse fibrillations.
Normal — important: HIV-associated sensory neuropathy would show sensory abnormalities; these are absent.
Reduced CMAP amplitudes. Normal conduction velocities. No conduction block.

quantitative_data.hiv_neuropathy_features: ABSENT — no sensory NCS abnormalities, no distal symmetric pattern
quantitative_data.als_features: PRESENT — multi-region denervation, paraspinal involvement, UMN signs

specialized_test.impression: EMG confirms ALS in HIV-positive patient. The EMG pattern is consistent with ALS, not HIV-related neurological complications: (1) Motor-predominant denervation in multiple body regions with paraspinal involvement. (2) Normal sensory NCS — HIV-associated sensory neuropathy would show sensory abnormalities. (3) Combined UMN signs on clinical examination (Hoffman, Babinski) inconsistent with HIV vacuolar myelopathy pattern (pure UMN) or HIV neuropathy (pure sensory/LMN). ALS concurrent with well-controlled HIV is the diagnosis.
recommended_actions: Continue ART — HIV control essential; ART does not cause this EMG pattern

interactions: Bictegravir (integrase inhibitor): metabolized primarily by CYP3A4. Riluzole is CYP1A2 substrate. Minimal direct DDI. Coadministration is feasible.
Tenofovir alafenamide: renal elimination, no CYP1A2 interaction.
warnings: Monthly LFT monitoring for riluzole. Note: biktarvy components can affect liver enzymes — baseline LFTs and close monitoring critical
Consult HIV pharmacist to confirm no interactions with specific ART regimen
alternatives: AMX0035 — check with HIV specialist for any ART interactions

output.interpretation: Opening pressure: 14 cmH2O. WBC: 3 cells/uL (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 48 mg/dL. Glucose: 62 mg/dL (ratio 0.66). NfL: 6,180 pg/mL (markedly elevated). Oligoclonal bands: Absent. HIV RNA CSF: Undetectable — HIV well-controlled in CNS. CMV PCR CSF: Negative.

results.title: ALS in HIV-infected patients
results.finding: Case reports and series describe ALS in people living with HIV. HIV does not cause ALS but can co-occur. Well-controlled HIV with undetectable viral load effectively rules out HIV-driven motor neuron disease. Management is same as HIV-negative ALS patients.

results.title: HIV neurology differential diagnosis — motor weakness
results.finding: HIV motor weakness ddx: vacuolar myelopathy (posterior column MRI changes), HIV-associated neuropathy (sensory predominant), CMV radiculomyelopathy (CD4<100), PML (white matter lesions). ALS with fasciculations, LMN+UMN combined, paraspinal denervation not characteristic of any HIV complication.

output.summary: ALS and HIV can co-exist independently. Well-controlled HIV (undetectable VL, CD4>500) with this clinical/EMG pattern is consistent with ALS, not HIV complication. Continue ART; add riluzole.

output.interpretation: Abnormal values: ALSFRS-R total score 37 points (H).

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) concurrent with well-controlled HIV infection

differential.key_feature: Vacuolar myelopathy causes posterior column degeneration with sensory and UMN findings; does NOT cause fasciculations, LMN denervation on EMG, or arm atrophy; MRI shows no vacuolar changes
Requires CD4 <100 for CMV reactivation; CD4 here is 520; CMV PCR negative
HIV neuropathy is sensory-predominant and symmetric distally; normal sensory NCS here excludes HIV neuropathy as explanation
Normal lactate; normal sensory NCS; current regimen (bictegravir/TAF) has very low mitochondrial toxicity

optimal_actions.action: HIV viral load and CD4 count — assess immune status and risk for opportunistic complications
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Undetectable VL, CD4 520 — well-controlled HIV; low risk for opportunistic CNS complications

optimal_actions.action: MRI brain and spine with gadolinium — assess for HIV myelopathy, PML, lymphoma
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Corticospinal tract ALS changes; no vacuolar myelopathy; no PML; no lymphoma

optimal_actions.action: CSF including HIV RNA, CMV PCR, NfL
optimal_actions.expected_finding: HIV RNA undetectable; CMV negative; NfL markedly elevated

optimal_actions.action: EMG/NCS with attention to sensory NCS pattern
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Normal sensory NCS (excluding HIV neuropathy); multi-region motor denervation (ALS)

optimal_actions.action: Check riluzole interaction with ART regimen

critical_actions: Assess HIV status (VL, CD4) first — well-controlled HIV effectively excludes HIV-driven opportunistic neurological complications
CSF including HIV RNA, CMV PCR to exclude HIV-related CNS complications
Normal sensory NCS is key — HIV neuropathy is sensory; ALS is purely motor
Continue ART — HIV control is essential; ALS does not alter HIV management need
contraindicated_actions: Attributing all neurological symptoms to HIV without EMG confirmation — HIV mimics are excluded systematically by well-controlled viral load, normal sensory NCS, and EMG pattern
Changing ART regimen based on neurological presentation — current regimen (Biktarvy) is appropriate and undetectable VL should be maintained
key_reasoning_points: HIV with undetectable viral load and CD4 >500 essentially excludes all HIV-driven opportunistic CNS complications that require immune deficiency
HIV neuropathy is sensory-predominant; ALS is purely motor — normal sensory NCS is the key distinguishing finding
Fasciculations and combined UMN/LMN syndrome are not features of any HIV complication; they are hallmarks of ALS
ALS concurrent with HIV is an independent co-occurrence; HIV treatment continues independently

red_herrings.data_point: HIV-positive status and history of opportunistic neurological complications in other patients
red_herrings.intended_effect: Attribute progressive weakness to HIV-related neurological complication (vacuolar myelopathy, HIV neuropathy, CMV)
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Well-controlled HIV (undetectable VL, CD4 520) makes HIV-related opportunistic CNS complications highly unlikely. Pattern of weakness with fasciculations and combined UMN/LMN signs is ALS, not any HIV complication.

metadata.notes: ALS in well-controlled HIV patient. Systematic exclusion of HIV-related neurological complications required. Normal sensory NCS and combined UMN/LMN pattern confirms ALS.
